correctness.rationale: For any finite connected metric graph of total arclength L and total bridge-edge length B, a level with a single transverse crossing must be in an edge whose interior removal disconnects G, so its image-level measure is <=B. The edgewise one-dimensional area formula yields pushforward density >=N(y)/L, hence the inverse quantile Q is absolutely continuous with derivative 0<=h<=L and excess ∫(2h−L)_+ <=B. The Brownian-bridge covariance kernel K(s,t)=min(s,t)−st turns Var(Q(U)) into positive quadratic form. Maximization over 0<=z<=1, ∫z=B/L forces a bang-bang indicator (strict positive definiteness), whose first-variation potential solves −Hʺ=1+1_A and is strictly concave, so A is one interval; equal edge heights force the central interval. Integrating the unique optimal quantile gives ((L+B)^3−4B^3)/(48L), attained by balanced two-cycle barbell and limiting circle/path. Independent symbolic integration verified the extremal density/variance polynomial; the unrestricted conclusion is analytic and does not follow from finite tests.

value.rationale: A sharp universal functional inequality depends only on two canonical metric-graph statistics, L and the total disconnection-edge length B. The theorem quantitatively interpolates the bridgeless circle and pure tree/path variance constants, constructs extremal network geometries for every feasible bridge fraction and uniquely determines the extremal output law. It answers an intrinsically useful geometry-to-Lipschitz embedding norm question.

scientific_limitations: Real-valued globally 1-Lipschitz observables and normalized uniform arclength only.
Universal envelope for prescribed L,B; not an optimal constant for each fixed graph nor full equality-geometry classification.
